mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the document's country of origin, or consular legalization at a South African High Commission or Embassy where the origin state is not a Hague Convention member

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founding shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners as 'prominent influential persons' (PIPs) per FICA Schedule 1 (as amended 2022) and FIC Guidance Note 7; mandatory cross-verification against the OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and domestic designations under POCDATARA and FIC directives; enhanced due diligence and source-of-funds verification required for foreign PIPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and any transaction route involving sanctioned shipping, port, or stevedoring counterparties; ongoing transaction monitoring and beneficial ownership register maintenance at CIPC

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal - https://eservices.cipc.co.za (Company Name Reservation, Form CoR 9.1 and CoR 9.2)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in any one of the 11 official South African languages but must be expressible in Latin/Roman script; non-Latin scripts and foreign-language names require an English transliteration approved by CIPC; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, and a translated/transliterated name must accompany the application where the primary name is not English; all statutory documents may be filed in English, the default filing language of the Companies Regulations, 2011
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Mutual Bank, or Building Society (requires Banks Act 94 of 1990 registration and Registrar of Banks approval)
Insurance, Insurer, or Underwriter (requires Prudential Authority licensing)

Offensive, obscene, defamatory, or xenophobic words prohibited under s 11 of the Companies Regulations, 2011
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A CIPC name reservation is valid for 20 business days from the date of the reservation, during which the incorporation application must be lodged; a once-only extension of 20 business days may be applied for before expiry under Regulation 11(4) of the Companies Regulations, 2011. Upon rejection of a name application, the applicant must first request a written statement of reasons from the CIPC within the prescribed period, then file an administrative objection/review with the Companies Tribunal under s 160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 within 60 business days of the CIPC decision, or alternatively re-apply with a revised name via Form CoR 9.3; the applicant may additionally institute a civil application in the High Court of South Africa if the Tribunal route is exhausted

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially acceptable. A virtual office address satisfies the registered office requirement under s 23 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 for incorporation and initial correspondence; however, for a bulk port stevedoring terminal operator, full commercial substance is mandatory: a functional operational office inside the port precinct, physical attendance capability, dedicated management personnel in South Africa, and a leased terminal or berth area are required by the Ports Regulator of South Africa and Transnet National Ports Authority (TNPA) for the statutory Stevedoring/Terminal Operator licence; pure virtual-office substance will trigger licence refusal and SARS de facto place-of-effective-management challenges
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - approximately 60% to 70% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 18 months of licensing, given that bulk port stevedoring is a controlled facility under the National Ports Act 12 of 2005, the ISPS Code maritime security regime, and routine SARS Customs excise and FIC compliance examinations; CIPC may also physically verify the registered office and records

incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account requirement. Shares may be issued at no par value and subscribed consideration may be nominal.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) The subscription and issue of [●] ordinary no-par-value shares of the Company to the subscribers named in the register of members, against payment of R[●], be and is hereby approved, ratified and allotted in accordance with the Memorandum of Incorporation. (2) The registered office of the Company, being [●] Street, [●], South Africa, be and is hereby adopted as the statutory registered and business address. (3) The following officer appointments be and are hereby approved: [Name] as Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Name] as Financial Director; and [Name] as Company Secretary, each effective immediately. (4) Management is authorised to file the Notice of Incorporation and to effect all ancillary statutory obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services Corporate Name Reservation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-search of the CIPC company name database via e-Services to confirm availability. File Form CoR 9.1 (Name Reservation) listing up to three preferred names in order of priority. Ensure the selected name contains the mandatory suffix '(Pty) Ltd'. The reservation is valid for 20 business days and may be extended once by filing a further application.
required_dossiers: Certified ID copies of all proposed directors and incorporators
Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, file a fresh CoR 9.1 with alternate names within the statutory window, or lodge a name consideration application with the CIPC; a dispute may be escalated to the Companies Tribunal under section 160 of the Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) by all incorporators, select the standard MOI or bespoke MOI, and complete Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation). File both documents electronically via CIPC e-Services and pay the prescribed incorporation fee. Upon approval, CIPC issues the Registration Certificate and assigns a unique company registration number.
required_dossiers: Certified ID copies of directors and incorporators
Declaration of registered office and business address
Proof of payment of incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried, rectify the defects and resubmit within 10 business days; a rejected application may be re-filed online or appealed to the CIPC by written objection within the prescribed review period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Tax Registration (Income Tax, VAT, PAYE, UIF and SDL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax via SARS eFiling using Form ITREG. Apply for VAT registration on Form VAT 101 where taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed ZAR 1 million per annum. Register as an employer on Form EMP 101 for PAYE, UIF and SDL compliance. Obtain a SARS tax compliance status PIN.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: SARS may query incomplete submissions; rectify director profiles and supporting documents and resubmit via eFiling; disputes may be lodged under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 through an internal objection followed by a formal appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Compensation Fund and Unemployment Insurance Fund Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (DEL) — Compensation Fund and UIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the Compensation Fund under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA) using Form CF 1, and with the Unemployment Insurance Fund using Form UIF-8. Registration must occur within 7 days of appointing the first employee. Submit a payroll declaration and confirm workplace safety arrangements.
required_dossiers: Expected employee headcount and payroll schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is rejected due to inadequate payroll data, submit corrected schedules and a formal written explanation to the Compensation Fund; late registration penalties may be remitted upon good-cause application under the COIDA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Transnet National Ports Authority (TNPA) as licensing authority under the National Ports Act, 12 of 2005, with regulatory oversight by the Ports Regulator of South Africa
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Stevedoring and Terminal Operator Licence under the National Ports Act, 12 of 2005 and TNPA Port Regulations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Authorisation (Scoping and Environmental Impact Assessment Report) required for new terminal construction or expansion under Listing Notice 2, Activity 15 of the EIA Regulations, 2014 (NEMA); existing stevedoring operations typically require registration for listed waste management activities and an Atmospheric Emission Licence (AEL) where applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with National Water Act, 36 of 1998 wastewater discharge limits; National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act, 39 of 2004 AEL thresholds for particulate matter (PM10/PM2.5) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs); MARPOL Annex V waste handling provisions; Department of Water and Sanitation harbour water quality guidelines; and hazardous waste management under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act, 59 of 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the local Fire Services Authority; structural load and crane/plant inspections by the Department of Employment and Labour under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 85 of 1993 (Major Hazard Installation Regulations); COIDA Certificate of Good Standing; terminal occupation certificate for operational buildings; and an approved Emergency Response Plan cleared by the TNPA Port Manager.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — eFiling portal: https://www.sarsefiling.co.za; official website: https://www.sars.gov.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: After incorporation of the (Pty) Ltd through the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), the entity must register for income tax with SARS via eFiling or a SARS branch, obtaining a South African Income Tax Reference Number. VAT registration is compulsory if taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any rolling 12-month period. Voluntary VAT registration may be made where taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 in a 12-month period. Foreign-owned entities must appoint a local representative taxpayer for SARS purposes and may be required to furnish security for VAT registration. A non-resident entity must register as a VAT vendor where it carries on an enterprise in South Africa and has a South African bank account or other prescribed security arrangements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not have a US-style check-the-box regime. A (Pty) Ltd is automatically a separate corporate taxpayer. Available elections relevant to a company include: voluntary VAT registration and VAT group registration under section 50 of the VAT Act; small business corporation (turnover-based) income tax elective regime under section 12E of the Income Tax Act (subject to turnover limits and activity exclusions); controlled foreign company (CFC) allocation or exclusion elections under section 9D of the Income Tax Act for foreign subsidiaries. No hybrid entity pass-through election is available for a South African private company under South African tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) — Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 in taxable supplies in any rolling 12-month period; voluntary registration may apply once taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 in a rolling 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently mandate a real-time continuous fiscal clearance, digital stamping or government API clearance regime for all VAT invoices. Tax invoices must satisfy the prescribed particulars in section 20 of the VAT Act. Electronic tax invoices are permitted subject to integrity, authenticity and duplication controls. VAT returns and supporting documentation are submitted through SARS eFiling and e@syFile channels; the SARS Customs environment operates separately through the SAD500 electronic customs declaration system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated for VAT if supplied to a non-resident and physically exported from South Africa within 90 days of supply (or such extended period as SARS permits), provided no subsequent re-import occurs. Services may be zero-rated under section 11(2) of the VAT Act where they are supplied directly to a non-resident and are not directly connected with immovable property in South Africa or movable property situated in South Africa at the time of supply. Stevedoring services supplied directly to a non-resident vessel operator or non-resident cargo owner for the loading of bulk cargo destined for export may qualify for zero-rating where the cargo is cleared for export by SARS Customs and the documentary evidence chain is complete. Services rendered to local freight forwarders, consignors or South African resident principals will generally be standard-rated at 15%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SARS Customs Export Declaration (SAD500 or electronic equivalent via SARS Customs e-filing)
Bill of Lading (original or certified electronic copy)
Commercial invoice for the exported cargo
Packing list or cargo tally sheet
Stevedoring/terminal outturn report or vessel load confirmation
Inward Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 bank credit advice evidencing foreign payment receipt
Berth order and port terminal service order tying the stevedoring service to the exported goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may disallow the zero-rating and retrospectively assess standard-rate VAT if the export documentation is deficient or the goods do not leave South Africa within the prescribed period. The clawback also carries interest from the due date of the original return. Under the Tax Administration Act, understatement penalties may apply on a sliding scale from 0% to 200% of the understated tax, depending on conduct (reasonable care, substantial non-compliance, gross negligence, or intentional evasion). Administrative non-compliance penalties may also be imposed for failure to keep satisfactory records. Deliberate fraudulent export VAT evasion may result in criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment in terms of the VAT Act and the Tax Administration Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), administering the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961 (Government Notice R1111, as amended, effective from 1 January 2021 under the exchange-control modernisation regime) together with the Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand (ZAR) is free-floating and fully convertible for current-account transactions; authorised dealer banks hold delegated authority to process service-related external payments (stevedoring fees, charter-hire, agency commissions) upon documentary review without individual FinSurv consent. Capital-account convertibility is liberalised but subject to reporting and source-of-funds verification: inward foreign direct investment (equity subscription or shareholder loan) is permitted and is registered on an inward investment file at the receiving authorised dealer; outward repatriation (dividends, loan redemptions, disinvestment proceeds) is permitted after (i) submission of an auditor's certificate in the prescribed 'External Income Remittance' template evidencing realised profits, (ii) satisfaction of South African dividend withholding tax at 20% (treaty relief may apply under an applicable DTA), and (iii) a SARS tax-compliance status PIN. There is no profit-remittance licence or annual ceiling; the operative constraint is documentation completeness rather than statutory quotas. The material practical hurdles are: (a) proving the provenance of the non-resident sponsor's funds (12-month bank statements plus corporate transcript), (b) reconciling the inward investment file before any later disinvestment, and (c) complying with the 180-day settlement rule on export services (terminal stevedoring invoices to non-resident shipowners).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For the ISIC 5224 stevedoring model, port-handling fees invoiced to non-resident vessel owners are treated as exports of services. Statutory timeline: the full invoice value must be received by the (Pty) Ltd within 180 days from the date of the service invoice (the authorised dealer may extend to 365 days upon documented justification, such as bulk-commodity discharge cycles). Mandatory conversion ratio: nil - the 2021 exchange-control modernisation abolished the historical requirement to surrender foreign currency to the authorised dealer within 30 days of receipt. The receiving dealer must credit the funds to the company's Foreign Currency Account (FCA) or ZAR account; the funds may be retained, converted to ZAR at market rate, or applied to authorised payments without any percentage-selling obligation. The exporter must file the SARS/FinSurv service-export electronic declaration (the services equivalent of the goods EX1), attach the vessel performance/throughput certificate issued by the terminal or port authority, and close each collection to the underlying export file; any overdue receivable must be justified or the dealer may report an 'unpaid export' irregularity to FinSurv, attracting administrative penalties.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a standalone clearing solution; MODERATE as an auxiliary collection/FX layer partnered with a licensed domestic bank. Legal constraints: (i) an offshore e-money institution (EMI) is not an 'authorised dealer' under the Exchange Control Regulations and holds no ZAR clearing licence, so it cannot settle rand-denominated payments or provide the statutory inward/outward investment file; (ii) the Banks Act 94 of 1990 (section 11) prohibits any unlicensed entity from conducting 'the business of a bank' in South Africa - EMI wallet receipts must therefore be swept via SWIFT MT103 into the domestic FCA; (iii) for foreign shipping SPVs, an EMI multi-currency account can accelerate invoice collections, but source-of-funds traceability and BOP purpose-code reporting are still required at the point the funds cross into the ZA banking system; (iv) recommendation: use the EMI only for pre-clearing aggregation of US$/EUR receipts where the underlying service contract names ZA Pty Ltd as beneficiary, then clear daily into the tier-1 FCA; never use an EMI as the principal disbursement ledger for payroll or port dues.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA 38 of 2001 does not mandate a physical branch visit for corporate account opening; however, the practical KYC standards of the tier-1 banks require (a) a notarised and apostilled board resolution appointing signatories, (b) a completed beneficial-ownership schedule (Companies Amendment Act 22/2022 filing) identifying all natural-person UBOs, and (c) identity verification of foreign directors, which all major banks deliver via video-interview confirmation. Remote onboarding is therefore accepted for a 100% foreign-owned (Pty) Ltd, with the following exception: if no resident director or employee is appointed, the bank's FICA officer will require a physical meeting (branch or notary) to activate internet-banking credentials and debit/credit instruments. Recommended strategy: appoint one resident executive director (or a South African tax-resident non-executive director) as co-signatory; this reduces onboarding to 5-8 business days, satisfies the banks' operational KYC expectations, and removes the de facto physical-visit condition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: 100% foreign shareholding routed through an offshore parent or single-asset SPV, combined with a 'cash-intensive' terminal operation profile that is inconsistent with the declared low-risk stevedoring activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC company extract and memorandum of incorporation; complete beneficial-ownership register filed with CIPC; shareholders register; parent's constitutional documents and board minutes approving the investment; 12-month parent bank statements demonstrating source of wealth/funds; audited financial statements of ZA Pty Ltd (where available); FSCA-licensed introducer's FICA attestation for each foreign directorship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound disbursements to ship registries and flag-state service providers (Panama, Marshall Islands, Liberia, Singapore) or to the foreign parent for management fees, which may be misinterpreted as trade-based money laundering or export-proceeds leakage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed stevedoring/terminal handling agreement with each vessel owner; TNPA berth allocation and vessel schedule; bill of lading or electronic terminal manifest for each collection; itemised service invoices with hourly tariff annexure; agency/chandler contracts with proforma invoices; bank-form 'Application for Foreign Payment' with BOP purpose code; transfer-pricing documentation (OECD TP file) for all intercompany fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (Companies Act 71 of 2008, section 33; Companies Regulations, 2011)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary date of incorporation, on an annual basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-submission places a delinquency penalty on the CIPC account; failure to file annual returns for two consecutive years exposes the company to CIPC administrative strike-off, which requires restoration proceedings and may entail director disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Companies Act, section 56B, and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Filing platform and the company's Beneficial Ownership Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the annual return, within 30 business days after the incorporation anniversary; any shareholding or beneficial interest change during the year must additionally be filed within the prescribed change-notification window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file an accurate annual beneficial ownership confirmation is an offence under the AML/CFT framework and may result in fines, imprisonment, CIPC administrative sanctions, and adverse filing status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements (mandatory where the Public Interest Score is 350 or more or a regulatory licensing condition requires audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (where annual financial statement filing is mandatory or elected); otherwise retained at the registered office and made available to shareholders and regulators
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end; the annual financial statements and audit report must be approved and signed before that deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defaulting directors may be jointly and severally liable for resulting losses; non-compliance is an offence under the Companies Act and may trigger CIPC compliance notices, monetary penalties, and refusal to issue a certificate of good standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies where the Public Interest Score is 350 or more; where the Public Interest Score is between 100 and 349, an independent review is required unless a full audit is voluntarily adopted; a company operating under a Port Authority licence or other regulatory instrument may also be audited as a licence condition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or IFRS for SMEs, as adopted for South African companies; public-interest entities and companies with higher Public Interest Scores are required to apply full IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual return preparation, the directors must confirm that the Beneficial Ownership Register is complete and matches the CIPC-filed data; any share transfer or beneficial interest change during the year must be recorded in the statutory register and filed with CIPC within the prescribed change window, and the annual return serves as the annual confirmation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; previously 28%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday; targeted incentives include: Section 12B accelerated allowances for qualifying plant/renewable-energy assets; Section 12C wear-and-tear allowances for stevedoring machinery/equipment; Section 12I industrial-project allowance (qualifying investment ≥ ZAR 50 million) for port-terminal brownfield/greenfield expansions; Section 11D 150% super-deduction for approved R&D; Section 12H learnership allowance. Effective rate is lowered by these allowances, but no statutory exemption from the 27% headline rate applies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carry-forward, subject to the 80% set-off cap: for years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2022, an assessed loss may be set off against only 80% of taxable income (at least 20% of taxable income remains exposed to the 27% rate).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Company Income Tax Return) submitted through the South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling portal; provisional returns via IRP6 (eFiling) and monthly/periodic PAYE/VAT returns where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual ITR14 return; provisional tax estimates (IRP6) submitted twice a year (third voluntary top-up available); dividend tax returns (DTR02) monthly.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: ITR14 must be filed within 12 months after the company's financial year-end (SARS may impose an earlier deadline via a Request for Return). Provisional tax: first IRP6 payment six months after the start of the year of assessment; second IRP6 payment on the last day of the year of assessment; third IRP6 (top-up) payment within six months after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Entity identification (Name, Registered/CIPC number, SARS tax reference, YOA)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name ZA_PTY_LTD, CIPC registration number, SARS taxpayer reference, and the year of assessment being filed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Pty Ltd is a South African tax resident if incorporated in ZA or effectively managed in ZA; therefore the entity itself must file as a resident company regardless of foreign ownership. Non-resident shareholders do not file ITR14 for the company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicates whether the company is resident for tax purposes (resident if incorporated, managed, or controlled in South Africa).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company is managed from abroad but incorporated in ZA, it remains tax resident; the company must still disclose its full worldwide income. Non-resident status applies only where the company is managed and controlled abroad and not incorporated in ZA (not the case for a ZA Pty Ltd).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Income: gross income, exempt income, and total receipts/accruals
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose all gross receipts from stevedoring, terminal-handling, loading/unloading, storage and ancillary port charges, in the relevant boxes for South African and foreign-source income; disclose exempt income separately.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign-source income as well; a tax credit (under section 6quat) may be claimed for foreign taxes paid on such income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the gross taxable turnover from marine cargo handling operations and select the SARS Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) code corresponding to ISIC 5224 (cargo handling/stevedoring).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that fees charged to foreign shipowners or non-resident charterers are reported as South African-source services income (source is where the service is rendered, i.e., the South African port).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Deductions and allowances (operating expenses, capital allowances, assessed loss relief)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim deductible operating expenses, section 12C/12B/12I capital allowances on cranes, conveyors, terminal equipment, and infrastructure, plus any assessed loss brought forward subject to the 80% set-off cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-related payments (management fees, royalties, interest) must be supported by transfer pricing documentation and must not be deducted if not actually incurred and arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxable income and tax computation at 27%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income (gross income minus deductions and allowances) and the amount of income tax at 27% before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No rate distinction applies to non-resident-owned Pty Ltd companies; the entity-level 27% rate is applied to worldwide taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Dividends declared and dividend tax payable (section 64H)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule all dividends declared to shareholders, the dividend tax withheld at 20%, and the applicable exemption/treaty-rate declarations (D&U forms) retained for non-resident shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For foreign shareholders claiming a reduced DTA rate (typically 5% or 15%), the company must obtain a valid Declaration and Undertaking and retain the shareholder's tax residence certificate before paying the dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offsets against the annual tax are provided for the first, second and (if elected) third provisional tax payments made during the year of assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to non-resident shareholders; the company claims its own IRP6 credits. Underestimated provisional tax exposes the company to the section 234 underestimation penalty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file: administrative non-compliance penalty under section 210 Tax Administration Act 28/2011 of ZAR 250 to ZAR 16,000 per month (depending on turnover) per outstanding return; late payment penalty under section 211 of 10% of the unpaid tax, plus interest at the SARS prescribed rate under section 187. Estimated assessments under section 95 may be raised. Understatement penalties under sections 222-225 range from 10% (substantial understatement) to 150% (intentional evasion); criminal prosecution for repeated or fraudulent non-filing may attract fines up to ZAR 10 million and/or imprisonment up to 10 years.
